went_well: Player-coach delivery finished D1-D11 in one context, with the board, gates and RTM kept as the accountability record

Mechanical gates caught real defects: s07/s08 notes over their time budget, a shell route around the PCI hook, a NaN alignment bug in the FRED loader, a gate-week mismatch between the evaluation plan and the charter
Sprint 1 output reused as-is: 89 sourced claims, the slide spec and the rollout plan
One consolidated review found 3 blockers and 9 majors that self-checks missed (an untrue audit claim, unconditional contract wording, a CI script injection); all fixed and held by a scripted re-check
went_badly: Sprint 1 fan-out spent about 2.3M subagent tokens for one accepted IC ticket; context loading dominated the cost
Three agent-drafted strategy documents were overwritten by mistake; restored from git, the compact versions kept as -card.md
A factual error about default permissions reached the slide spec before the register (CLM-606) corrected it
improvements: Scale agents with output, not with the org chart: one author, machine gates, one independent reviewer
Give any agent a small context pack (the brief and one ADR), never the whole playbook
Check git status before writing to paths another agent owns
Facts enter the claims register before they enter a spec
Run the independent review before publishing, not after: two republishes of the deck could have been one

review.note: Measured: consolidated review 372,793 subagent tokens (one Sonnet pass); headless Claude Code runs about $2.71 (G3 dry-run $2.30, hook verification $0.01, reviewer checks about $0.20, re-verification about $0.20). The placeholder-resolution subagent was not metered. Compare Sprint 1: about 2.3M subagent tokens for one accepted IC ticket.
